newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korea agrees to arrange peace talks-sources.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea agrees to arrange peace talks-sources.

text.p: North Korea has agreed to a meeting of senior officials with South Korea, the United States and China to arrange four-way peace talks, Seoul government sources said on Wednesday.

"Pyongyang has accepted a suggestion that senior officials from the two Koreas, the United States and China meet around early August to set an agenda and other details for the peace talks," a source said.

The peace talks, proposed jointly by the United States and South Korea, aim to close the books on the 1950-53 Korean War by replacing a fraying armistice with a permanent peace treaty between the capitalist South and the Stalinist North.
The sources said senior officials from the two Koreas and the United States would first meet in New York early next week to announce an accord for the "preparatory talks".
Seoul foreign ministry spokesman Lee Kyu-hyung declined to confirm the North Korean agreement but said: "There will be an announcement on four-way peace talks at 10:00 p.m. (1300 GMT) today."
South Korean Foreign Minister Yoo Chong-ha has said that he is "cautiously optimistic" over the prospects of holding peace talks this year.
